summary:
# NOTES: *The Lady of the Forest: A Story for Girls* (L. T. Meade, Gutenberg #39705)

Epigraph: "Tyde what may betyde, / Lovel shall dwell at Avonsyde." Family motto over tower arch.

## SETTING
- Avonsyde: old Lovel house, New Forest, Hampshire. Tower (~700 yrs old), modern wings. Straight avenue of oaks/beeches, winding avenue to stone porch. Forest with bogs, Jack-o'-lanterns, Rufus' Stone, bluebell glade with giant oak, Nancy's cottage (green-covered, rose porch) deep in forest.
- Lovels held Avonsyde ~800 yrs. Rupert Lovel laid first stone under William Rufus. ~1684: Squire disinherited elder son Rupert (left 20 Aug 1684) and gave estate to younger son Valentine.
- Melbourne suburb house "Belmont" (Australia). Southampton (post office, railway). London: Baring & Baring, 128 Chancery Lane (lawyers); Jermyn Street hotel; Waterloo station; Lyndhurst Road station; Mrs. Lovel's London lodging: No. 10 Abbey Street, Marshall Road, S.W.

## CHARACTERS
- **Rachel Valentine Lovel** (dark, gypsy-faced, tall, bold, romantic, loves fairy tales; ~12–13; birthday 5 May; wants to go round world seeking mother; Surefoot = her grey pony; Ruby = red-coated spirited pony; Jupiter = terrier; calls Kitty "Kitty-cat").
- **Kitty (Katharine) Lovel** (fair, golden hair, blue eyes, pink-white, sweet, affectionate, ~9 at start; loves Phil; fishes; her pet spaniel).
- **Aunt Griselda "Grizel" Lovel** (Miss Griselda; elder, cold, strong-minded, admires Rupert; practical; wants to find heir; sharp tongue; crochet).
- **Aunt Katharine "Kitty" Lovel** (Miss Katharine; younger, tender-hearted, sympathetic, music/organ gift, knits; sister's shadow).
- **Squire Lovel** (old father of the sisters; dying; will requires search for male heir: Rupert's descendant, strong, manly, boy, lineal descent, under 15).
- **Valentine Lovel** (sisters' brother, died of consumption; married low-born Bella/Mrs. Lovel).
- **Mrs. Bella (Rachel) Lovel** (née Rachel Cunningdale; Valentine's widow; mother of Rachel and Kitty; milliner; weak-willed but loving; made lace; £400 saved; 6 years apart; sold diamond ring for £10; in old Australia she is the Phil's mother; lives in forest cottage as "lady of the forest"; secretly stole tankard & letters from Belmont).
- **Philip "Phil" Lovel** (son of Mrs. Bella & Philip Lovel [Australian, died in railway accident]; age 8; pale, freckled, slight upturned nose, beautiful brown eyes; secret heart/side pain; "Spartan"; loves spiders, caterpillars; calls Rupert "dearest friend"; nurse Betty; gardener Jim; dog Cato; mother's nickname "mammy").
- **Newbolt** (Mrs. Newbolt, lady's-maid; loves Phil, detests Mrs. Lovel).
- **Nancy White** (old servant/nurse of the lady of the forest; keeps the tankard; "ain't"; hid tankard; wears straw-colored... no—wears shawl, striped jersey; wrote couplet "False heirs never yet have thriven; / Tankards to the right are given").
- **Robert** (young groom; mother ill; "missy"; rides with children).
- **Mrs. Martin** (housekeeper). **Mr. Eyre / John Eyre** (forest agister); **Mrs. Eyre**; **Peter**; **Canning** (servant).
- **Dr. Maddon** (family doctor). **Mr. Terry** (Barings' country partner). **Mr. Baring** (younger lawyer, ~30) & elder Mr. Baring.
- Marmaduke family (London; Mrs. & Mr. Marmaduke; daughter Clementina ~13 (fat face, riding pride, Captain Delacourt lessons, Margaret & Jessie Dawson friends), sons Dick and Will, youngest Abby; pug dog; parrot; lady's-maid).

### Belmont (Australia) family
- **Rupert Lovel** (elder brother's son; ~15; tall, strong, dark eyes, brave, mother died; father is Rupert Lovel senior, brother of Philip). Rupert's siblings: **Gabrielle** (13, stately, grave, housekeeper, boudoir), **Peggy** (little, flaxen hair, ravens Elijah & James Grasper). Dead mother of Rupert/Gabrielle/Peggy.
- Mr. Davis: family business friend.

## KEY OBJECTS
- **Silver tankard**: Lovel crest, motto "Tyde what may" (engraved); kept in "sacred cupboard" behind mother's bed at Belmont; proof of descent. Mrs. Bella stole it (and letters) on visit to Belmont. Phil found it in old horsehair trunk in tower room; took it into forest; lost near bog. Nancy found and kept it. Later returned to Rupert.
- **Letters**: proof of descent; stolen along with tankard.
- **Old diary** (vellum-bound; "book-case marked D") recording the quarrel.
- **Ring**: Rachel's gold ring with pearl given to lady of forest via Nancy; Mrs. Bella wears it.
- **Lace**: Mrs. Bella makes; crochet/knitting.
- **Phil's horn cup, "Robinson Crusoe"** (lost/missing).
- Newspaper advert: "Lovel.--If any of the lineal descendants of Rupert Lovel ... Messrs. Baring & Baring... Only heirs male in direct succession need apply." Sisters' advert: "...provided the said descendant be under fifteen years of age and of sound physical health."

## CHRONOLOGY (plot)
**Ch.I**: Rachel tells fairy story to Kitty in forest; Aunt Grizel interrupts; sends Kitty to Eyres; mentions Phil coming. Background of Avonsyde & family history. Squire Lovel dying; sets heir conditions; sisters promise. Kitty kisses his hand. Rachel & Kitty burst into his bedroom. Squire recognizes Rupert-look in Rachel; Kitty = Valentine's weak look (per Griselda). Squire kisses; says "I wish to God, child, you were a boy!"
**Ch.II**: Mother (Bella) in hallway waits; "make terms." Sisters: Katharine demands welcome; Griselda agrees children must stay; mother will be obliterated. Terms: children stay; mother leaves; no interview content revealed. Squire dies that night after blessing kiss from Kitty & Rachel ("Rupert's child").
**Ch.III** (5 years later): Kitty & Rachel discuss incoming heir Philip (age 8). Rachel's mother-longing. Griselda had searched America. Griselda says if boy strong she's relieved; Katharine doubts mother's letters.
**Ch.IV**: Phil & mother on train from Southampton; mother coaches lies (no Betty/Jim/cottage). Phil's spider; arrival; Kitty welcomes him; Rachel goes to forest. Mrs. Lovel says born in Mexico, moved to America, then Australia. Griselda considers her; "pedigree".
**Ch.V**: Kitty & Phil in woods; Phil wants fish; Rachel rides Surefoot alone to forest; Robert protests. Rachel meets Newbolt/Nancy at lady's cottage; lady in dark dress fled from her. Nancy: lady lonely, must keep secret; Rachel promises (not Kitty). Rachel reveals to Nancy Phil & Kitty etc.
**Ch.VI**: Tower bedroom described (octagon, four-poster, winding stair, oak door). Newbolt: heir always slept there. Mrs. Lovel distressed. Phil mentions Rupert; mother fears. Phil reveals he loves Rupert; mother says they must leave; last £20.
**Ch.VII**: Belmont (Melbourne) scene: Rupert, Gabrielle, Peggy. Phil's letter (dated; posted Southampton; asks reply to post office Southampton, "to be called for"). Aunt Bella mysterious. Betty (O'Flanigan) reads letter. Father Mr. Lovel: advert in Melbourne Times; sail for Europe Saturday; tankard & letters needed; tankard swapped with fake (no crest/motto; not silver). Gabrielle: "It is the 4th of November."
**Ch.VIII**: Gabrielle searches mother's sacred cupboard; Rupert in mother's room; tankard missing. Rupert: "I shall never love Avonsyde as I love Belmont."
**Ch.IX**: Rachel's trysting-place; Nancy: "lady" appears at Rachel's 13th birthday (5 May). Rachel gives ring to Nancy for lady; plans to bring Phil.
**Ch.X**: Mrs. Lovel gets £500/year offer; "Am I not to live at Avonsyde always?" Griselda: heir proclaimed; search continues; tankard, proofs.
**Ch.XI**: Children tell tales; Phil wants money. Phil plans; night: finds tankard in mother's horsehair trunk. Dawn: goes into forest.
**Ch.XII**: Phil lost; bog; robins lead lady to him.
**Ch.XIII**: Phil wakes in lady's cottage; she gives hot milk, hen Brownie's egg; Phil thinks she's the lady of forest; asks for bag of gold; lady: "I am no supernatural lady... plain woman... earns bread." Nancy returns; Mrs. Bella & Nancy talk (lace; six years; "I made up my mind the day Kitty fainted"); Nancy hides tankard.
**Ch.XIV**: London: Mr. Baring (younger) meets Mrs. Lovel; Australian Rupert Lovel (senior) and young Rupert recognize her ("Rachel Cunningdale"). Mrs. Lovel tells full backstory (father died in debt; married Valentine; two girls; Nancy White nurse; sold ring; arrived Avonsyde; terms with sisters; term-of-years Rachel's 13th birthday). Young Rupert says he doesn't want Avonsyde.
**Ch.XV**: Phil & Kitty in armory; Phil's pain; mother rescues; Rachel knows his secret (lady in gray took him home); Rachel to Phil: "Phil, what happened in bog..." Mrs. Lovel tells Phil they've "almost won" on 5 May; Phil wrote Rupert asking for reply at Southampton.
**Ch.XVI**: Backstory of Mrs. Lovel's weakness; husband Philip killed in railway accident; Phil's pain since age 6; advert seen; Rupert's wife's (Belmont) cupboard; mother asks to go to Southampton; retrieves letter; learns tankard lost (Phil had it in bog). "We are utterly lost!"
**Ch.XVII**: Phil alone; plans to look for tankard; Rachel & Phil conspire about visiting lady's house during Marmadukes' visit. Marmadukes arrive (ten days).
**Ch.XVIII**: Marmadukes; Clementina; Rufus' Stone picnic; Clementina rides Ruby; Phil visits cottage (Nancy: lady not at home); asks about tankard.
**Ch.XIX**: Phil walks with lady of the forest; she lets Phil lead her; Rachel sees her face. Rachel & Phil talk; Rachel declares she'll go round world at 15. Clementina lost on Ruby.
**Ch.XX**: Clementina thrown into bog; Robert & Phil find her; Phil lectures her; Phil rests in "nest"; Clementina & Mrs. Lovel confrontation; Miss Griselda & Katharine intervene.
**Ch.XXI**: Marmadukes leave. Griselda grows fond of Phil; Phil says heir should be like Rupert ("picture"). Griselda: 5 May date; Katharine says mother will come 5 May.
**Ch.XXII**: Rupert senior & Rupert junior in London; Rupert: "Right is right"; decides no claim until tankard/letters; 5 May deadline. Mrs. Lovel tells Nancy about lost tankard; Nancy's guilty reaction.
**Ch.XXIII**: Spring; forest life; Phil's happiness; Nancy meets Phil, admits hiding tankard in her cupboard.
**Ch.XXIV**: Griselda (Mrs. Lovel letter) — invites mother for 5 May at No. 10 Abbey Street; Mrs. Lovel summoned to library; Griselda reads diary; asks for tankard; Mrs. Lovel flees; goes into forest; sleeps by oak; Nancy writes couplet on paper.
**Ch.XXV**: Phil's dream: lady of the forest offers "gift" (beauty & heart); takes him to Fairyland; says rightful heir coming 5 May. Mrs. Lovel decides to give Avonsyde to Rupert.
**Ch.XXVI**: Mrs. Lovel letter to Griselda; telegrams (Mr. Baring); Mrs. Lovel goes to London, confesses to Mr. Baring; they go to find Rupert.
**Ch.XXVII**: Lady of forest's cottage; Rupert & Baring arrive; Mrs. Lovel confesses; Mrs. Bella (lady) & Mrs. Lovel meet. Evening: Katharine plays organ; Phil asks "Play joyfully"; Phil & Griselda talk: "lady of the forest... comes to every one some day."
**Ch.XXVIII**: 5 May party at Avonsyde. Mrs. Lovel in black velvet; crimson rose. Guests; Mr. Baring's arrival; lady of forest arrives with Rachel & Kitty; Rupert arrives; Mrs. Lovel confesses to all guests; Phil and Rupert talk in forest; Phil dies on Rupert's shoulder, seeing "lady" in vision. Final line: "That is the story. Sad? Perhaps so--not sad for Phil. THE END."

## NOTABLE QUOTES
- "Tyde what may betyde, Lovel shall dwell at Avonsyde."
- Squire: "I wish to God, child, you were a boy!"
- Mrs. Bella: "I am willing to obliterate myself."
- Phil: "I'll be a Spartan boy and bear the pain."
- Phil: "I want the bag of gold so badly."
- Rachel: "Oh, it is good of God to make such a beautiful world!"
